en: This man is better than that man.
la: Hic vir melior est quam ille.
explain: The comparative adds “more”: _bonus_ (good) becomes _melior_ (better). It is irregular, like English good, better, best.
distractors: Hic vir bonus est quam ille.
Hic vir optimus est quam ille.
Hic vir meliōrem est quam ille.
_meliōrem_ is accusative. The subject needs the nominative: _melior_.

en: The girl is better than the boy.
explain: After a comparative, _quam_ means “than”, and the two things compared stand in the same case: _puella … quam puer_ (both nominative).

en: The girl is better than the boy (no quam).
explain: Instead of _quam_, the thing compared can go in the ablative: _puerō_ (than the boy). It is common when the second thing is short.
distractors: _puerum_ is accusative. After a comparative without _quam_, use the ablative: _puerō_.
_puer_ is nominative. Without _quam_, use the ablative: _puerō_.
_puerī_ is genitive or plural. Without _quam_, use the ablative: _puerō_.

explain: _magnus_ (big) has the comparative _maior_ (bigger). It agrees with _liber_: masculine nominative.

en: This city is bigger than that city.
la: Haec urbs maior est quam illa.
explain: _maior_ is the same for masculine and feminine. _quam illa_ means “than that one”.
distractors: Haec urbs maximus est quam illa.
Haec urbs magna est quam illa.
Haec urbs maius est quam illa.

explain: The superlative is “most”: _bonus_, _melior_, _optimus_. It agrees with _vir_ (masculine nominative).
_magnus_, _maior_, _maximus_: big, bigger, biggest. _maxima_ is feminine to agree with _urbs_.
_malus_ (bad) becomes _peior_ (worse). The neuter nominative is _peius_, to agree with _hoc_.
distractors: _peior_ is masculine or feminine. _hoc_ is neuter: _peius_.

explain: _parvus_ (small) has the comparative _minor_. It agrees with _numerus_ (masculine).
_magis_ is the adverb “more”: it says how much you do something. It does not change for case or gender.
distractors: _maior_ is an adjective, “bigger”. To say how I love, use the adverb _magis_.

en: You work better than I do.
explain: The adverb for “better” is _melius_. It describes how you work, so no agreement is needed.
distractors: _melior_ is an adjective, “better” of a person. For how you work, the adverb: _melius_.
